title: Introduction to Old English Language and Literature
description: Introduction to Old English language and literature. Students learn to read and translate a selection of prose and verse works. A full description for any given quarter will be available on the English Departments website.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10; upper-division standing.

title: Old English Literature: Beowulf
description: Reading, analysis, and interpretation of the Old English poem Beowulf in the original language. Acquaints students with a variety of critical approaches to the poem. A full course description for any given quarter will be available on the English Departments website.
prerequisites_raw: English 110A.

title: Readings in Old English Literature
description: Study of Old English literature, in the original language. Course contents vary from quarter to quarter. To see what is being taught in any particular quarter, students should consult the course listings on the English Departments website.
prerequisites_raw: English 110A.

title: Old English Literature in Translation
description: Study of Old English prose and verse texts in translation. Considers the history, theory and practice of translating Old English literature. Course contents vary from quarter to quarter: to see what is being taught in any particular quarter, students should consult the course listings on the English Departments website.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or upper-division standing.

title: The History of the English Language
description: English in its old, middle, and modern forms. Such introductory topics as language families and change; etymology, semantics; grammars; syntax; oral,written; groundwork for such methods of literary analysis as stylistics.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10; upper-division standing.

title: Practical Criticism
description: A combined writing and criticism course for students of literature.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10 or upper-division standing.

title: Sharing Private Journaling: A Writing Paradox
description: In this special one-unit course, Professor Shirley Lim will guide students in the craft of journaling. Students who aspire to record and listen to themselves, and, if they wish, to share their Muses' little and large observations will find a safe space in this small seminar. Students will approach why, what, when, where, and how to journal as singular voices whose collective work will be shared in a course publication.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10 or upper-division standing.

title: Studies in Literary Theory and Criticism
description: Explorations in traditions and innovations of critical theory, literary interpretation, and philosophy. Topics vary from quarter to quarter, but will focus on the major critical figures or movements (from Aristotle to the present) that have shaped our notion of literature.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10; upper-division standing.

title: Early Modern Women Writers
description: This course looks at writing by women published between 1650 and 1780. We’ll read and talk about a range of genres: poems, novels, scandal memoirs, a few essays. A guiding question: when did the idea of ‘women’s writing’ emerge, and how was it defined — and is the category still relevant for how we write and publish today?

title: Medieval Women's Writing
description: This course focuses on works of medieval women's writing from the twelfth to the fifteenth century. We consider the ways that these texts work in and against premodern structures of gendered power, and the new formal and aesthetic possibilities opened up by the marginalized positions that these writers occupied. Core texts include Marie de France's Fables, The Wooing of Our Lord, Julian of Norwich's Revelations of Divine Love, and The Book of Margery Kempe.
prerequisites_raw: Writing 2 or upper-division standing.
